T: No cats in America. Plenty of cheese.
D: A young mouse emigrates to New York and gets separated from his family.
P: Serve the cheese when Fievel arrives in New York.
S: Crisp grated potato and onion pancakes with sour cream and apple sauce. Grate 6 medium potatoes (about 800g) and 1 onion and squeeze out the liquid.
little meat pies from the old country
Yeasted dough wrapped around beef, onion and dill filling, fried or baked at 200C until golden.
the Mousekewitz family's taste of the old country

Potato and cheese dumplings boiled then fried in butter with golden onion, served with sour cream and dill. Mash 500g boiled potatoes with 100g grated cheddar and salt. Cut 24 rounds from 2 sheets fresh pasta or use gow gee wrappers, fill each with a spoon of potato, fold and press shut. Boil in batches for 3 minutes until they float. Fry 1 sliced onion in 40g butter until golden, add the dumplings and toss 2 minutes. Serve with 150g sour cream and dill.
M: Beetroot, cabbage, carrot and potato simmered in beef stock with a splash of vinegar and dill, sour cream on top.
Mama's cheese blintzes with berry sauce
Mama Mousekewitz's cooking, carried from Shostka to New York

Thin crêpes rolled around sweet lemon ricotta, fried golden in butter and served with warm berry sauce and sour cream. Whisk 150g plain flour, 3 eggs, 350ml milk and a pinch of salt. Cook 8 thin crêpes in a buttered pan, one side only. Mix 400g ricotta, 100g cream cheese, 50g sugar and lemon zest. Fill the cooked side, fold into parcels and fry in 30g butter for 2 minutes a side. Simmer 300g frozen berries with 2 tbsp sugar for 5 minutes and serve with sour cream.
W: a Hanukkah sweet from back home in Shostka

Honey, oil, eggs, brown sugar, coffee and spices beaten into flour, baked at 170C for 50 minutes. Whisk 250g honey, 125ml oil, 3 eggs, 150g brown sugar and 125ml strong coffee. Fold in 300g flour, 2 tsp baking powder and 2 tsp mixed spice. Pour into a lined tin and bake at 170C for 50 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
K: the samovar's on while Papa plays violin

Black tea brewed strong and poured into glasses with lemon slices and a spoonful of jam to sweeten. Brew 4 tsp black tea in 1L just-boiled water for 4 minutes and strain into 4 heatproof glasses. Add a slice of lemon to each and serve with 100g raspberry jam for stirring in instead of sugar.

note.text: Papa said there are no cats in America. Papa was wrong, but I am still going to find him.

winks: Fievel lost overboard in a bottle during the storm
Tiger the cat, the friendly one
Henri the pigeon and his French accent
Warren T. Rat, the con artist

steps.text: Grate the potatoes and onion and squeeze out the liquid well.
Mix with the eggs, flour and salt.
Fry spoonfuls in hot oil until crisp, turning once. Work in batches.
Serve with sour cream and apple sauce.
Mix the flour, yeast, warm milk, sugar and butter into a soft dough and knead briefly.
Cover and let the dough prove.
Fry the mince with the chopped onion and dill.
Cool the filling.
Cut the dough into rounds, fill, and seal.
Bake at 200C until golden.
Grate the beetroot and carrots, shred the cabbage and dice the potatoes.
Simmer all the vegetables in the stock until tender.
Add the vinegar and plenty of dill.
Serve with a big spoon of sour cream and rye bread.
Heat the oven to 170C and line a tin.
Whisk the honey, oil, eggs, sugar and coffee.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and mixed spice and pour into the tin.
Bake until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin.
Brew the tea in just-boiled water and strain into heatproof glasses.
Add a lemon slice to each and serve with jam for stirring in.

s.how: Grate 6 medium potatoes (about 800g) and 1 onion and squeeze out the liquid. Mix with 2 eggs, 3 tbsp flour and salt. Fry spoonfuls in oil for 3 minutes a side until crisp and serve with 150g sour cream and 200g apple sauce.

s.note: little meat pies from the old country
s.how: Mix 400g flour, 7g yeast, 250ml warm milk, 1 tsp sugar and 30g butter into a soft dough and prove an hour. Fry 400g beef mince with 1 onion and dill, then cool. Fill 12 rounds of dough, seal and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.

m.how: Grate 3 beetroots and 2 carrots and shred a quarter cabbage. Simmer with 2 diced potatoes in 1.5L beef stock for 40 minutes. Add 2 tbsp vinegar and plenty of dill. Serve with a big spoon of sour cream and rye bread.

w.note: a Hanukkah sweet from back home in Shostka
w.how: Whisk 250g honey, 125ml oil, 3 eggs, 150g brown sugar and 125ml strong coffee. Fold in 300g flour, 2 tsp baking powder and 2 tsp mixed spice. Pour into a lined tin and bake at 170C for 50 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.

d.note: the samovar's on while Papa plays violin
d.how: Brew 4 tsp black tea in 1L just-boiled water for 4 minutes and strain into 4 heatproof glasses. Add a slice of lemon to each and serve with 100g raspberry jam for stirring in instead of sugar.
